Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

htna 0.3.6

  • build_htna() has a time argument naming the column with the time of each event. With it the events are ordered by time and the order column is not needed. It makes method = "latency" of Nestimate 1.0.20 available, a network in which each reply is weighted by its speed.
  • summary() of an undirected network (method = "co_occurrence") counts each edge once, in the header and in the actor-pair table, which has one row per unordered pair of actor types. The counts agree with the network metrics of Nestimate 1.0.7 and later and with as.data.frame().
  • print() of a centrality_stability_htna() result says when whole actors were dropped (actor), and its plot labels the axis accordingly.
  • certainty_htna() keeps the actor types on its result, and plot_htna_bootstrap() draws it.
  • Help pages name the settings recent Nestimate versions added: nested mosaics, target for case-dropping reliability, format for association rules, and the estimation methods "reverse", "ngram", "gap" and "latency".

htna 0.3.5

This section covers all changes since the CRAN release 0.3.1.

New features

  • bootstrap() and plot_sequences() reach the htna methods whichever of htna and tna is attached last: the methods are also registered on tna’s generics of the same names. Through tna::bootstrap(), tna’s argument names (level, method, threshold) are mapped onto those of bootstrap_htna() (ci_level, inference, edge_threshold).
  • centrality_stability_htna() passes further arguments to Nestimate::centrality_stability() through ..., as the other wrappers do, so Nestimate’s actor argument (resample whole actors) reaches it.
  • Result objects have tidy accessors. as.data.frame() returns the edges (with the actor types of source and target) or the nodes of an htna network or grouped network; the tables of a summary() (what = "actors", "actor_pairs", "metrics"); the actor-pair, edge, metric and network tables of a compare_htna() result; and the CS coefficients or correlation traces of centrality_stability_htna(). Grouped results are stacked with a group or comparison column.
  • compare_htna() results have print() and summary() methods; a grouped comparison prints one block per cohort pair instead of the raw list.
  • Grouped bootstraps (bootstrap_htna() on an htna_group) have print() and summary() methods, and grouped stability results a summary().
  • plot_htna_diff() draws a grouped bayes_compare_htna() result, one difference network per cohort pair.
  • Errors are classed conditions inheriting from htna_error (htna_bad_input, htna_missing_column, htna_actor_conflict, htna_unassigned_node, htna_empty_input, htna_missing_package, htna_unnamed_nodes), documented in the Conditions section of each help page.

Changes

  • summary() of an htna network or grouped network returns a summary.htna / summary.htna_group object that prints the same report; it no longer prints as a side effect of the call.
  • build_htna(group = ) returns the cohorts in the order of the levels when the grouping column is a factor (for human_ai, Early then Late), so grouped comparisons are named "Early vs Late". Character grouping columns keep their previous order.
  • build_htna() detects a code used by two actors also when there are three or more actor types and the code is not used by all of them.
  • as.data.frame() on an htna network now returns htna’s edge table (with actor columns) instead of cograph’s.
  • The centrality stability plot uses the Okabe-Ito palette, distinguishes the measures by line type and point shape as well as colour, titles each cohort’s chart with the cohort name, and raises a classed error when ‘ggplot2’ is not installed.
  • Unused suggested packages ‘codyna’ and ‘janitor’ were removed.

Documentation

  • Help pages were rewritten to describe the method each function implements, with return structures, conditions and runnable examples on the bundled data. Examples no longer reach into result objects.
  • New vignette “Grouped heterogeneous transition networks”; the main vignette sets out the model and a complete analysis.
  • New guides “Comparing networks” and “Sequences and patterns” (replacing the sequence plot and sequence comparison articles), and two case studies on the vibe-coding sessions. “Input formats” is now a guide on the package website.
  • The examples of sequence_plot_htna() and plot_sequences() use one project, so they run quickly when the ‘stringdist’ package is not available.
  • Corrected return-value documentation of markov_order_test_htna(), sequence_compare_htna(), state_distribution_htna(), pruning_details_htna() and plot_htna() (0.3.2).

Tests

  • The shipped tests no longer compare against ‘Nestimate’ or ‘tna’; those comparisons moved to a local equivalence suite. The Edge Count test of summary() follows the network’s directed flag, for CRAN ‘Nestimate’ and ‘Nestimate’ 1.0.7 or later (0.3.3, 0.3.4).

htna 0.3.1

CRAN release: 2026-07-28

Fitted MMM conversion

  • build_htna() now explicitly consumes the fitted net_mmm object returned by Nestimate::cluster_mmm(). It materializes one HTNA network per fitted sequence cluster without rerunning MMM and preserves assignments, posterior probabilities, mixing proportions, information criteria, fitted weights, and the original actor partition.
  • Nestimate::as_htna() now supports the same fitted net_mmm input and returns an equivalent htna_group. Nestimate::cluster_network() remains the function that directly returns materialized cluster networks.

Datasets

  • New per-actor long frames human_simplified and ai_simplified, ready for the named-list form of build_htna().
  • New tidy code → actor-type lookup human_ai_codebook, ready to pass as node_groups to build_htna().
  • human_ai gains a phase factor column tagging each session as "Early" or "Late" (chronological split), so grouped examples can call build_htna(human_ai, group = "phase") without pre-processing.

Documentation

  • htna_palette is now exported (previously an internal constant referenced as a default argument in exported plot functions).
  • New article vignette Clustering inputs to build_htna() covering Nestimate::build_clusters() and Nestimate::cluster_mmm(), model selection with cluster_choice() / compare_mmm() / cluster_diagnostics(), and cohort-pair comparison with compare_htna().

htna 0.3.0

Actor-aware interoperability and comparison

  • Added compare_htna(), an actor-aware wrapper over Nestimate::compare_model(). It aligns partial node coverage, annotates every edge with source and target actors, reports summaries for each actor-pair block, retains the original HTNA networks, and compares every cohort pair when passed an htna_group.
  • Added as.igraph() methods for htna and htna_group. Converted graphs preserve actor types as vertex attributes and canonical actor ordering as graph metadata; grouped inputs convert every cohort.
  • summary.htna() and summary.htna_group() now include Nestimate’s standard network-level descriptive metrics alongside the existing actor-partition and actor-to-actor edge summaries.
  • build_htna(method = "co_occurrence") is now documented and covered across all constructor forms, grouped networks, MCML expansion, Nestimate distance clustering, and legacy TNA clustering, with numerical equivalence tests against both Nestimate and tna::ctna().

htna 0.2.2

MCML expansion

  • build_htna() now accepts a fitted Nestimate::build_mcml() object. The MCML node clusters become actor groups, and one full node-level HTNA is rebuilt from the retained or explicitly supplied original source. This is equivalent to Nestimate::as_htna(): it intentionally preserves global cross-cluster transitions rather than stitching together fitted macro or within-cluster weights.
  • HTNA partition injection now consistently stores character labels in $node_groups$group and a factor with the full actor level set in $nodes$groups.

htna 0.2.1

Verification

  • Added extensive randomized equivalence coverage for constructing HTNA models from Nestimate distance clustering, fitted mixed-Markov clustering, and legacy tna clustering results, including actor-partition preservation and no-refit guarantees.

htna 0.2.0

New features

  • build_htna() now consumes Nestimate distance clustering (net_clustering), fitted MMM clustering (cluster_mmm() / net_mmm), materialized cluster networks (netobject_group), and legacy tna::cluster_sequences() results. It returns an htna_group, restores the actor partition on every child, and preserves clustering assignments, posterior probabilities, diagnostics, and fitted MMM weights. A partition preserved upstream is used automatically; older or independently-created clustering results can supply node_groups.

Six htna-named functions are added, extending htna’s coverage of the major transition-network-analysis (tna) verbs. All are thin ...-forwarding wrappers over the ‘Nestimate’ engine and follow the same durable design as the existing re-exports (stable documented formals; new engine arguments flow through ...).

  • Pruning family — prune_htna(), deprune_htna(), reprune_htna(), and pruning_details_htna() (over Nestimate::net_prune() and friends). The actor partition and htna class are preserved across pruning, so the pruned network stays htna-aware and plots with [plot_htna()].
  • bayes_compare_htna() — Bayesian complement of permutation_htna() (over Nestimate::bayes_compare()). Preserves the actor partition on $x/$y and carries class net_permutation, so it renders with plot_htna_diff().
  • certainty_htna() — closed-form counterpart of bootstrap_htna() (over Nestimate::certainty()), joining the confirmatory-analysis family alongside reliability_htna() and casedrop_reliability_htna().

htna 0.1.2

  • The six re-exported Nestimate functions (permutation_htna(), association_rules_htna(), casedrop_reliability_htna(), markov_order_test_htna(), state_distribution_htna(), state_frequencies_htna()) are now thin ...-forwarding wrappers instead of direct aliases. Their documented formals are fixed, so a future change to any of these functions’ signatures in Nestimate can no longer produce a code/documentation-mismatch (codoc) WARNING in R CMD check. No behavioural change: each call forwards unchanged to Nestimate (including S3 dispatch for state_distribution_htna()), and extra arguments pass straight through ....
  • sequence_compare_htna() no longer restates Nestimate’s sequence_compare() arguments (sub, min_freq, test, iter, adjust) as its own formals; they now pass through .... Its signature is x, group, level, ... — the htna-specific level argument is retained. Same defaults and behaviour, but new Nestimate arguments flow through automatically and the code/documentation coupling is removed. mosaic_plot_htna()’s documentation is likewise decoupled from Nestimate’s signature (it was already a ... wrapper).

htna 0.1.1

  • Compatibility with Nestimate 0.8.0. Nestimate::permutation() gained a measures argument (for centrality permutation tests); since permutation_htna() re-exports that function, its documentation is regenerated to include the new argument, resolving a code/documentation mismatch flagged by R CMD check. No behavioural change.
  • Imports: Nestimate (>= 0.8.0).

htna 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-07-06

  • Initial release.
  • Builds heterogeneous transition networks for sequences mixing two or more actor groups (e.g. Human and AI) within the same interaction, via build_htna().
  • Re-exports the most commonly used Nestimate and cograph downstream functions under _htna-suffixed aliases so callers do not need to attach Nestimate or cograph explicitly: permutation_htna(), casedrop_reliability_htna(), markov_order_test_htna(), mosaic_plot_htna(), state_distribution_htna(), state_frequencies_htna(), association_rules_htna(), sequence_compare_htna().
  • htna-side wrappers add ergonomics over the upstream API: frequencies_htna(), plot_frequencies_htna() (treemap / bars / facet views), centralities_htna(), plot_centralities(), plot_htna(), plot_htna_bootstrap(), plot_htna_diff(), sequence_plot_htna(), reliability_htna(), centrality_stability_htna(), edge_betweenness_htna(), extract_meta_paths() (state-level by default; level = "type" for the type-level meta-path rollup; supports schemas mixing types, concrete codes, and *).
